[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Saving provision] The amendments contained in the 181 st Update to Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot do not apply to claims that –

## SECTION 1 – DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

## 1.1 Definitions

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “affordability calculation” means a calculation made electronically by the court, by applying a formula to information submitted by the parties. The explanation of the formula is set out in Annex A. The purpose of the calculation is to establish what rate of repayment of an amount of money that a defendant is likely to be able to afford;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “affordability calculation repayment plan” means a plan that sets out the rate of repayment established by the affordability calculation. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “all proceedings order” means an “all proceedings order” under section 42(1A) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “alternative response” has the meaning given by paragraph 9.1;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “bulk scanning provider” means the bulk scanner supplying scanning services via the OCMC postal address set out at paragraph 2.1(2)(a);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “CNBC” means the Civil National Business Centre;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “civil proceedings order” means a “civil proceedings order” under section 42(1A) of the Senior Courts Act 1981;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “civil restraint order” means an order restraining a party from –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (a) making any further applications in current proceedings (a limited restraint order);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (b) issuing certain claims or making certain applications in specified courts (an extended civil restraint order); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (c) issuing any claim or making any application in specified courts (a general restraint order);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “claimant” means the person who makes an online claim against another person;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “contact details” means a party’s email address and/or telephone number;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “CTSC” means the Courts and Tribunals Service Centre at Stoke on Trent;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “the defendant” means the person that the claimant is making the claim against;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “defendant’s home court” means the County Court hearing centre serving the address where the defendant resides or carries on business;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “directions” means an order by the court dealing with procedural matters, for example an order setting out the dates by which certain steps must be taken;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “enter judgment” means the court makes and records a judgment;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “Help with Fees” means remission or part remission of a fee prescribed by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] HMCTS” means HM Courts and Tribunals Service;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “legal adviser” has the meaning given in paragraph 1.2(b) of Civil Procedure Rules Practice Direction 2E – Jurisdiction of the county court that may be exercised by a legal adviser;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “legal representative” has the meaning given in Civil Procedure Rule 2.3(1);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] MyHMCTS” means the online case management tool managed by HMCTS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “OCMC email address” means the address for submitting documents by email, where the document is in electronic format that cannot be uploaded, or cannot be converted to be uploaded, to the OCMC website set out at paragraph 2.1(2A)(a) or (b) as appropriate;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “OCMC postal address” means the address for submitting documents in paper copy set out at paragraph 2.1(2)(a) or (b) as appropriate;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “the OCMC website” means the website that hosts Online Civil Money Claims and that can be found at the following website address: www.moneyclaims.service.gov.uk (opens in a new tab) , and accessible for claimants acting in person at www.gov.uk/make-money-claim, and for defendants acting in person at www.gov.uk/respond-money-claim (opens in a new tab) , and accessible for legal representatives through MyHMCTS;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “online application” means an application made using the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “online claim” is a claim that is allowed by paragraph 2.1(3) of this practice direction to be brought using the Online Civil Money Claims process;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “online claim form” means the claim form that has been completed using the relevant screens on the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “online directions questionnaire” means the questionnaire that the parties complete and submit using the relevant screens on the OCMC website to tell the court about their hearing requirements, should a court hearing be necessary;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “paper response form” means Form OCON9X Form N9A and N9B, that is sent in paper copy to a defendant who is unable to respond to the claim using the OCMC website, which that defendant must use to respond on paper instead;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] preferred court” means –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (a) if the defendant is not an individual and the claimant has submitted an online directions questionnaire, the county court hearing centre specified in the claimant’s online directions questionnaire; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (b) in all other cases, the county court hearing centre specified in the defendant’s online directions questionnaire;”;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “protected party” has the meaning given in Civil Procedure Rule 21.1(2);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “regulated agreement” has the meaning given in section 189 of the Consumer Credit Act 1974;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “repayment plan” means the plan that sets out the terms that a claimant or defendant may propose for the repayment of an amount of money. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “response form” means:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (a) in the case where all the parties are acting in person, the relevant form that a defendant who is able to use the OCMC website must use to provide the detail of their response to the claim and as set out in Table A to paragraph 5.1(3);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] (b) in the case where the claimant is legally represented (irrespective of whether the defendant is legally represented), the response form that has been completed using the relevant screens on the OCMC website;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “stay”, in relation to proceedings, means a halt in proceedings, apart from taking any steps allowed by the Civil Procedure Rules including this practice direction or allowed by the terms of the stay. If the stay is “lifted” by the court, it means that the proceedings are allowed to resume;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.1 Definitions] “trial bundle” means the collection of documents (including statements of case and witness statements) that a party intends to rely on at the trial or hearing where the claim is decided. ## 1.2 Interpretation – “completion” of forms, and signing of forms

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2 Interpretation – “completion” of forms, and signing of forms] 1.2(1)For the purposes of this practice direction, a party completes a form by completing all parts of the form that are relevant to the proceedings that the party is involved in. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 1.2 Interpretation – “completion” of forms, and signing of forms] 1.2(2) If a person is required to sign a form, that form is signed by that person entering their name in the required field in an online form, or manually signing or typing their name at the appropriate place on a paper form. ## SECTION 2 – SCOPE OF THE PILOT

## 2.1 Scope of this Pilot

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] 2.1(1) The purpose of this practice direction is to establish a pilot to test an online claims process, called “Online Civil Money Claims”. Sub-paragraph (3) sets out the conditions that need to be met for a claim to be within the scope of the pilot. Where a claim is within the scope of the pilot-

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (a) Claimants who are not represented by a legal representative may use the pilot to make their claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (b) If the claimant is legally represented, the pilot must be used to make the claim if sub-paragraph 2.1(5A) applies. The pilot is to run from 7th August 2017 to 6th April 2027. The pilot applies in the County Court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] 2.1(2) Claims started using Online Civil Money Claims will be issued in the CTSC and will proceed there under the pilot unless they are sent out of the pilot. Normally, documents should be submitted to the court electronically using the “OCMC website” (as defined) or if it cannot be submitted using the website, then by email in accordance with sub-paragraph (2A). However, if this is not possible, the address for submitting documents in paper copy is-

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (a) HMCTS CMC, PO Box 12747, Harlow, CM20 9RA; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (b) where the parties have received an order from a judge at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, the postal address for that hearing centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (2A) Where parties are required by this practice direction to email the court,or where a party is to submit to the court a document that is in electronic format but that cannot be uploaded, or cannot be converted to be uploaded, to the OCMC website, the document should be sent by email to –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (a) the email address supplied for the CTSC; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1 Scope of this Pilot] (b) where the parties have received an order from a judge at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, the email address stated for that hearing centre on the “Find a court or tribunal” webpage which can be found at: Find a court or tribunal – GOV.UK. (opens in a new tab)

## 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (a). the claim is a claim for a specified amount of money only;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (b). the claim would not ordinarily follow the Part 8 procedure;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (c). the claim is not being brought under the Consumer Credit Act 1974 unless it is brought under section 141 of that Act, to enforce a “regulated agreement” (as defined) relating only to money;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (d) subject to subparagraph (7), either—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (i). the claimant will not be getting help with bringing the claim from a “legal representative” (as defined) and the claimant believes that the defendant will not be getting help with defending the claim from a “legal representative”; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (ii) the claimant and the defendant are each represented by a legal representative who is registered with MyHMCTS, and the claimant will not, before submitting their claim, apply for remission or part remission of a fee prescribed by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (iii) the claimant is represented by a legal representative who is registered with MyHMCTS, the claimant believes that the defendant will not be getting help with defending the claim from a “legal representative”, and the claimant will not, before submitting their claim, apply for remission or part remission of a fee prescribed by the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (e).
